newsitem.title: USA: NHL-SABRES GOALIE HASEK APOLOGIZES TO WRITER FOR CONFRONTATION.
newsitem.headline: NHL-SABRES GOALIE HASEK APOLOGIZES TO WRITER FOR CONFRONTATION.

text.p: Injured Buffalo Sabres star goaltender Dominik Hasek on Monday apologised for a physical confrontation with a sports columnist after a loss to the Ottawa Senators Friday night, the team said.
Hasek, who missed his team's last three playoff games because of sprained right knee, met privately with Buffalo News columnist Jim Kelley, the Sabres said.
A statement released by the team said Hasek "expressed his sincere apologies and regret" to Kelley and that the goalie will make a public statment on the matter later this week.

The altercation, which took place in the hallway at Buffalo's Marine Midland Arena, stemmed from a column Kelley wrote last week which questioned the severity of Hasek's injury and his desire to return to the Buffalo goal.

The All-Star goaltender, who carried the Sabres to a division title and is a leading candidate for the league's most valuable player award after posting 37 wins and a league-high .930 save percentage, was outraged by Kelley's column.
The two crossed paths on the way to the Buffalo lockerroom and Hasek stopped, spit on the floor and grabbed Kelley's shirtcollar with both hands.
Players and security officials quickly separated the two men, but Kelley's shirt was ripped in the confrontation. Kelley declined to comment on the incident.

The Sabres evened the best-of-seven series with the Senators with a 3-0 win on Sunday behind backup goalie Steve Shields. Sabres coach Ted Nolan will turn to Hasek if he is available to play Game 7 Tuesday night, but it is uncertain if Hasek will be ready.
Hasek suffered the injury in the second period of Game 3. He removed himself from the game and did not return, although he did stand on the bench in the third period in street clothes.

Kelley noted that Hasek was not on crutches and wore no brace or ice pack. Last Wednesday, the Buffalo News reported that team officials had been concerned over Hasek's "mental state" for days amid rumours of a rift with coach Nolan.

Hasek issued an angry statement last week saying he enjoyed the pressure of playoff hockey and that the injury was the only thing keeping him from playing. His teammates followed with a statement of support for their star goaltender.
